Article Title: Year-wise plan to implement Samudra Manthan in works
Article Text:
Petroleum minister Hardeep Puri reviewed the action taken on decisions from two brainstorming sessions on the rollout of the scheme, which received Cabinet’s approval, said officials. (Photo: IANS)

NEW DELHI: Government is likely to finalise a year-wise plan soon for drilling, seismic surveys and rig deployment under Samudra Manthan, a Rs 84,084-crore national programme aimed at stepping up oil and gas exploration in India’s offshore basins and reducing dependence on energy imports.Officials said petroleum minister Hardeep Puri recently reviewed the action taken on decisions from two brainstorming sessions held in Gurgaon in Haryana and Duliajan in Assam, on the rollout of the scheme, which received Cabinet’s approval last month.The year-wise roadmap will help government carry out exploration and production activities in a concerted manner across Krishna-Godavari (KG), Mahanadi, Andaman and Cauvery basins and ensure systematic utilisation of funds, an official said.The scheme will fund acquisition, processing and interpretation of seismic data, scientific drilling in frontier basins, accelerated exploration in deepwater and ultra-deepwater blocks, and development of shared offshore production and evacuation infrastructure.While Rs 43,200 crore has been earmarked for drilling 60 exploratory deepwater wells over five years, Rs 28,534 crore has been allocated for acquisition of 2D and 3D seismic data, Rs 10,000 crore for common infrastructure hubs and Rs 2,000 crore for an oil and gas manufacturing and services zone.India’s annual crude oil requirement is around 256 million tonnes (MT), of which nearly 88 per cent is imported. Domestic crude oil production from 26 sedimentary basins is estimated at around 28 MT. With domestic output stagnating even as demand continues to rise, government has been looking to step up exploration to improve energy security and reduce import dependence.Samudra Manthan is expected to add more than 600 million metric tonnes of oil equivalent (MMTOE) to the country’s hydrocarbon reserves and boost domestic production of crude oil and natural gas.Officials said government has implemented a series of upstream sector reforms over the past decade, including opening up almost the entire offshore acreage for exploration, changes to legal and contractual framework, and strengthening National Data Repository. Samudra Manthan would complement these reforms by providing public funding for offshore exploration and facilitating the deployment of advanced technologies, they said.The scheme also includes dedicated provisions for digital programme management, capacity building, technology adoption, stakeholder engagement and international outreach, creating an integrated ecosystem to accelerate offshore exploration and production in the country.
Article Summary: Samudra manthan is a rs 84,084-crore national programme aimed at stepping up oil and gas exploration in india’s offshore basins. The scheme will fund acquisition, processing and interpretation of seismic data, scientific drilling in frontier basins, accelerated exploration in deepwater and ultra-deepwater blocks.

Article Title: Wireless communication picked up; search operation launched in J&K's Samba
Article Text:
The hilly area of Sumb is considered strategically important from a security perspective. (PTI photo)

JAMMU: Security forces launched a joint search operation in the remote, hilly hamlet of Sumb in J&K’s Samba district after receiving information that a wireless set had been briefly activated in the area and satellite communication was detected around 1pm Tuesday.“The reported activation of Iridium satellite sets raised suspicion among security agencies, following which a combined team of the Army, police, and personnel from other forces rushed to Sumb’s Makoli village and initiated extensive searches in and around the area,” an official said Wednesday.“Terrorists often switch off such communication devices after contacting their handlers across the border,” said a source, adding that Iridium sets can be used on smartphones through the “Iridium GO!” mobile application, which creates a local Wi-Fi network that an iOS or Android phone can connect to.The operation continued until late Tuesday, but no satellite set or other suspicious material was found. Security was tightened along all routes leading to Sumb, with J&K Police and Village Defence Guards maintaining strict vigil, officials said.The hilly area of Sumb is considered strategically important from a security perspective as the route runs along the Basantar river and leads towards the India-Pakistan international border. Due to its proximity to the border, Samba district is a hotbed of terrorist activities. It serves as a gateway district for ultras heading towards Kashmir Valley via the upper reaches of Samba-Udhampur-Doda-Kishtwar.
Article Summary: Security forces launched a joint search operation in the remote, hilly hamlet of sumb in j&k’s samba district after receiving information that a wireless set had been briefly activated. Article Title: Travis Kelce’s $1.5 million nonprofit faces scrutiny after records show $469,000 spent on management and $446,000 on charity
Article Text:
Travis Kelce(Image via Getty Images)

Travis Kelce nonprofit spending comes under scrutiny

Travis Kelce foundation says tax filings were incorrect

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Earlier this year, Travis Kelce ’s reputation for giving back was facing a setback after an investigation into the NFL players’ charitable foundations raised questions about how some donated money was spent. Kelce’s Eighty-Seven and Running Foundation raised more than $1.5 million between 2021 and 2024, yet its reported charity spending was notably lower than that of several other NFL-linked organizations.In January, 2026, according to federal tax records examined by The Arizona Republic, Eighty-Seven and Running reported about $1.5 million in revenue during the three-year period and roughly $1.1 million in expenses. About $446,000 was listed under charitable spending, while $469,000 was reported as management costs.That works out to about 41 cents of every dollar spent going toward charity based on the filings. Charity Navigator generally views nonprofits spending at least 70 cents of each dollar on programs as efficient, while CharityWatch uses 75 cents as a benchmark for high efficiency.The figures have drawn attention partly because of the foundation's ties to A&A Management Group.The company was co-founded by Travis Kelce’s longtime business managers, Aaron and André Eanes. Aaron Eanes also serves as the nonprofit’s executive director.Laurie Styron, executive director of CharityWatch, raised concerns about the structure after reviewing the records.“It appears to function more as an extension of the management company versus as an independent public charity,” said Laurie Styron, the executive director of CharityWatch, an independent charity watchdog group that reviewed the nonprofit’s tax filings for The Arizona Republic.“That’s not how charities work. It’s wrong.”Travis Kelce’s team disputes the picture presented by the filings. Aaron Eanes said the reported figures did not properly classify some operational expenses tied to charitable work.“Operational costs for charitable efforts were “mistakenly reported under management rather than allocated adequately to program services,” Eanes told The Republic, so the public records do not provide an accurate “indication of where the resources were truly directed.”.Eanes said the foundation has since changed its approach, adding that management fees fell sharply in 2024 and reached zero in 2025. He also said the organization plans to expand its board, bring in nonprofit advisers and improve its reporting practices.“Looking ahead, we are expanding our board of directors, bringing on advisers with nonprofit expertise, and restructuring our reporting processes to better reflect our actual program work. We are dedicated to ensuring this foundation operates at the highest standards.”The scrutiny comes as the NFL continues to highlight charitable work through the Walter Payton NFL Man of the Year program. Kelce has been nominated three times and has supported causes in both Kansas City and his hometown of Cleveland.Kelce's foundation’s reported numbers do not erase that community work, but they do highlight why financial transparency matters. For celebrity-led nonprofits, public trust depends not only on how much money is raised, but also on how clearly and responsibly that money reaches the people it is meant to help.
Article Summary: Travis kelce ’s reputation for giving back was facing a setback after an investigation into the nfl players’ charitable foundations raised questions about how some donated money was spent. Kelce’s eighty-seven and running foundation raised more than $1.5 million between 2021 and 2024, yet its reported charity spending was notably lower than that of several other nfl-linked organizations.

Article Title: 'Intellectual dishonesty': SBI hits back at 2.6% GDP growth claim, says numbers compared incorrectly
Article Text:
SBI hits back at 2.6% GDP growth claim, says numbers were compared incorrectly

Dispute over the 2.6% figure

Real GDP growth would still be strong

Latest figures to be revised

The State Bank of India (SBI) has rejected claims that India’s nominal GDP growth in the first quarter of FY27 was only 2.6%, saying the figure came from comparing two different versions of the GDP data.The pushback came after former finance secretary Subhash Chandra Garg questioned the government’s reported 7.8% real GDP growth for Q1 FY27.Garg pointed to a revision in the previous year’s current-price GDP saying that Q1 FY26 GDP had been revised from around Rs 86 lakh crore to about Rs 80 lakh crore and argued that, without the revision, nominal growth would have been around 2.6%.Official data released by the ministry of statistics and programme implementation (MoSPI) showed real GDP growing 7.8% year-on-year in Q1 FY27. Real GDP at constant prices stood at an estimated Rs 81.36 lakh crore, up from Rs 75.46 lakh crore in Q1 FY26. Nominal GDP growth was reported at 10.3%.SBI said the 2.6% figure does not represent a valid comparison, rather it is "completely unsolicited and a sure sign of intellectual dishonesty.”The National Statistical Office (NSO) had estimated nominal GDP for Q1 FY26 at Rs 86.1 lakh crore when it released the quarterly figures on August 29, 2025.However, the August 31 release, prepared using the new GDP base year of 2022-23, revised the Q1 FY26 figure down to Rs 80 lakh crore.For Q1 FY27, nominal GDP was estimated at Rs 88.3 lakh crore.According to SBI, the 2.6% growth figure comes from comparing the latest Rs 88.3 lakh crore estimate with the older Rs 86.1 lakh crore figure for Q1 FY26, instead of using the revised number.“Some estimates are now ascribing a 2.6% growth in nominal GDP for the latest quarter instead of 10.3%, by calculating yearly growth rate using Rs 88.3 lakh crore (we call it A series in the adjacent table) over Rs 86.1 lakh crore (we call it C series). This is completely unsolicited and a sure sign of intellectual dishonesty,” SBI said.The bank said the latest Q1 FY27 figure should instead be compared with the revised Q1 FY26 figure under the new GDP series. That calculation gives nominal GDP growth of 9.7%.SBI also laid out an alternative comparison for those wanting to use the previous, unrevised Q1 GDP base. It said the Rs 88.3 lakh crore Q1 FY27 figure should be compared with Rs 80.4 lakh crore under the new base, rather than the old Rs 86.1 lakh crore estimate.“If anyone truly wants to compare current nominal GDP numbers over the previous unrevised base of Q1 GDP, then Rs 88.3 lakh crore (new base, A series) should be estimated over Rs 80.4 lakh crore (new base, B series), which comes out to 9.7% growth (as against 10.3%),” the report said.SBI said that the picture would remain positive even if nominal growth were calculated differently. It said that after adjusting the deflator under the alternative calculation, real GDP growth for Q1 FY27 would be 7.4%, compared with the officially released 7.8%.“Hypothetically, even with this nominal growth (by adjusting deflator), the real growth for Q1 FY27 would be 7.4% (as against released 7.8%), still good enough when looking at wall of exogenous challenges,” it said.The bank also stressed that GDP numbers are not final when they are first released. Quarterly estimates are revised over time and those revisions can move in either direction.SBI said that between FY22 and FY25, quarterly GDP data saw 25 upward revisions and 12 downward revisions.According to SBI, what made the latest revision different was that the National Accounts Statistics directly incorporated revised figures from previous years into the quarterly data.The bank said this was done to make the figures more transparent and to bring them in line with base revisions in the Consumer Price Index (CPI), Index of Industrial Production (IIP), Wholesale Price Index (WPI) and Producer Price Index (PPI).“This is perfectly legitimate,” SBI said.It added that aligning the bases helps keep GDP deflators and volume estimates consistent with the updated price and production indices.The bank also pointed out that the Q1 FY27 GDP estimate released in August 2026 is itself not final. The figure will go through further revisions and is expected to be finalised only by February 2029.“Revisions are part and parcel of a GDP number,” SBI said.SBI also rejected the claim that the change in the GDP base year had increased the size of India’s nominal GDP. According to the bank, the latest base-year revision had actually resulted in a lower nominal GDP size.
Article Summary: Sbi hits back at 2.6% gdp growth claim, says numbers were compared incorrectly. Former finance secretary subhash chandra garg questioned the government’s reported 7.8% real gdp growth for q1 fy27. Real gdp at constant prices stood at an estimated rs 81.36 lakh crore, up from rs 75.46 lakh crore.

Article Title: Indian Navy SATCOM : Indian Navy eyes indigenous SATCOM terminals to boost network-centric warfare
Article Text:
The Indian Navy is seeking to enhance network warfare capability through improved satellite communication technology. (Image credit: Indian Navy)

India Project 18 Destroyer: Japan’s Maya Technology Could Change India’s Navy

In the middle of a modernisation drive, the Indian Navy is seeking to improve its network centric warfare capability. The navy has floatted an Expression of Interest (EoI) for the development of indigenous ship-based satellite communication (SATCOM) terminals designed to work with its latest satellite, the GSAT-7R. The project, seeks a domestically developed and industry funded SATCOM system. The indigenously developed advanced C-band and Ku-band terminals will let warships maintain secure voice, data and video links even while operating thousands of kilometres out at sea.The Navy has been leaning on satellite communication since 2013, when GSAT-7 Rukmini first went into service. This satellite provided the fleet with a single secure network. This capability was significantly expanded with the launch of GSAT-7R, this satellite launched in November last year extends secure communication coverage to roughly 2,000 kilometres across the Indian Ocean Region. What the Navy wants now is for the ship-based terminals that talk through this satellite.The enhanced capability will allow the navy to strengthen its network warfare capability. This capability links different ship and aircraft into a single shared operational picture, so commanders across the force can see the same real-time data on enemy dispositions, own-force locations and emerging threats.Rather than each platform fighting in isolation the entire fleet is fused and distributed instantly across the network, letting any unit engage a target even if it wasn't the one that spotted the target.This capability was first demonstrated by the navy during Exercise TROPEX in 2014. Roughly 60 warships and 75 aircraft were connected into one network via the GSAT-7 Rukmini satellite, this resulted in faster decision-making and better coordination across a dispersed fleet. This provided the fleet with the ability to have different ships act as the sensor and the shooter platform.The system relies on Rukmini Terminals, the new systems are meant to reduce mechanical components wherever possible, improving reliability in harsh maritime conditions marked by constant rolling, pitching and yawing, salt-laden air, high winds and vibration. The programme will begin with three prototypes, a large C-band terminal, a large Ku-band terminal and a smaller Ku-band terminal, before moving to series production of around 30 units in total. As with other Make-II projects, companies will bear the full development cost themselves, with a minimum 50% indigenous content mandated across both hardware and embedded software, as per the EoI.Testing requirements are notably rigorous, including three-axis motion table trials to simulate real sea conditions and validate that the terminal can hold a stable satellite link, alongside evaluation at the Space Applications Centre in Ahmedabad and a mandatory vulnerability assessment clearance before integration into the Navy's network. The project has been reserved for MSMEs for now, with startups and consortiums of up to five members also eligible to participate. Companies have until 22 September to raise queries, with the EoI submission deadline set for 24 October, followed by a 104-week window to develop working prototypes.
Article Summary: The indian navy is seeking to enhance network warfare capability through improved satellite communication technology. The project, seeks a domestically developed and industry funded satcom system. The indigenously developed advanced c-band and ku-band terminals will let warships maintain secure voice, data and video links.

Article Title: Meta's highest-paid employee Alexandr Wang can't stop making fun of Google, says who is ...
Article Text:
Meta AI head

The benchmark behind Alexandr Wang’s dig at Google

Where the gains came from

The cost advantage

Alexandr Wang, Meta’s chief AI officer and highest-paid employee recently took a jab at Google ’s Gemini after a benchmark data shoed Meta’s latest AU model climbing near the very top of the industry rankings. In a post shared on social media platform X (formerly known as Twitter) Wang wrote, “I really hate to say it, but… gemini who? 🚀💨” alongside a performance chart showing Meta’s Muse Spark 1.3 surpassing several Gemini variants on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index. According to Artificial Analysis, Muse Spark 1.3 scored 62 points, placing it behind only Anthropic’s Claude Fable 5.1 (66) and Claude Opus 5 (63). The model outperformed Google’s Gemini 1.5 Pro and Gemini 1.5 Flash, which scored 61 and 53 respectively.Wang's comment was posted in response to a thread from Artificial Analysis announcing that Meta had released Muse Spark 1.3, the company's fourth Muse Spark model release in just five months. According to the benchmark firm, Muse Spark 1.3 (max) — currently in limited preview for Meta's partners — scored 62 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, trailing only Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Opus 5 in their top configurations.The publicly available variant, Muse Spark 1.3 (xhigh), scored 61 on the same index, putting it in a tie with GPT-5.6 Sol (max), Grok 4.6 (high), and Claude Opus 5 (high). That score represents a 4-point jump from Muse Spark 1.2's score of 57 in August, and an 8-point gain over Muse Spark 1.1's score of 53 in July. It landed just behind Claude Fable 5.1 (max, 66), Claude Opus 5 (max, 63), and Claude Fable 5 (max, 62).According to Artificial Analysis, both new Muse Spark variants improved primarily in two areas: agentic task performance and scientific reasoning.On agentic work, Muse Spark 1.3 (xhigh) posted a 12-point gain over Muse Spark 1.2 on the Tau3-Bench Banking evaluation, rising from 35% to 47%, along with a 5-point gain on Terminal-Bench 2.1 (80% to 85%) and a jump in GDPval-AA v2 Elo rating from 1,615 to 1,709. The limited-preview Muse Spark 1.3 (max) variant pushed even further, reaching 52% on Tau3-Bench Banking — the highest score of any model on that specific benchmark — and a GDPval-AA v2 Elo of 1,754. Artificial Analysis noted that Muse Spark 1.3 (max) achieves these higher scores in part by using significantly more reasoning tokens than the xhigh variant, reasoning 62% more on GDPval-AA v2 and 28% more on Tau3-Bench Banking.On scientific reasoning, the standout gain came on CritPt, where the xhigh variant improved 8 points over Muse Spark 1.2, from 18% to 26%. GPQA Diamond rose 4 points, from 90% to 94%, while Humanity's Last Exam and SciCode each posted more modest 2-to-3-point gains.Beyond performance, Muse Spark 1.3 also demonstrated efficiency. The xhigh variant costs about $0.55 per task, significantly lower than GPT‑5.6 Sol and Grok 4.6, which cost nearly double. Analysts noted this places Muse Spark on the “Pareto frontier” for intelligence versus cost, making it one of the most competitive models in terms of value.For those unaware, Meta has released four Muse Spark models in just five months, underscoring its aggressive push in frontier AI.
Article Summary: Muse spark 1.3 scored 62 points, placing it behind only anthropic’s claude fable 5.1 (66) and claude opus 5 (63) the model outperformed google”s gemini 1.5 pro and gemini 1-5 flash, which scored 61 and 53 respectively.

Article Title: Former Ukrainian Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov is launching a defense technology company backed by Palantir
Article Text:
Alex Karp backed defense company turning wartime experience into a product

A war reshaping military technology

Fedorov's abrupt exit from government

What Fedorov has been doing since leaving government

Palantir CEO Alex Karp stepping in as the first lead investor in a new defense technology company founded by former Ukrainian Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedoro. According to a report by CNBC, the size of Karp’s investment has not been disclosed, but Fedorov’s press office confirmed the partnership, saying details of cooperation with Palantir will be announced gradually. In a video posted by Fedorov on social media platform X (formerly known as Twitter), Karp praised the venture, saying it could bring Ukraine’s wartime knowledge and experience “as a product to allied countries.” He added: “You and your colleagues are launching a company that I think will be defining for the world.”The company’s name, specific technologies, and the extent of Karp’s involvement have not yet been disclosed. Palantir did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Fedorov’s office said the venture will build on lessons learned during Ukraine’s war with Russia, where drones, artificial intelligence, and battlefield software have played a critical role.The launch comes as Ukraine's ongoing war with Russia continues to accelerate the development and battlefield deployment of technologies including drones, artificial intelligence, and military software.Fedorov, long known as a vocal advocate for using technology to modernize Ukraine's military, said the new company would apply lessons learned during the war to build technology usable by both Ukraine and its allied partners.Fedorov, 35, said in a statement: “During the full-scale war, our team gained unique experience working with defense technologies in Ukraine and seeing firsthand how technology is transforming modern warfare.” He added that the company will aim to apply those lessons to products usable by both Ukraine and its allies.Fedorov, 35, was removed from his role as defense minister by President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in July as part of a broader government reshuffle, after serving in the position for just six months. His removal sparked public protests in Ukraine at the time.Since exiting government, Fedorov has been actively courting US investors and technology executives as he pursues a series of defense-focused ventures. He is separately seeking U.S. backing for a defense technology investment fund targeting areas including battlefield robotics, interceptor drones, and AI-enabled missile systems, according to a Financial Times report published last week.Fedorov built relationships with several prominent U.S. tech executives during the war. Last month, he described Elon Musk as the most important tech figure and entrepreneur in the world for Ukraine, crediting Starlink's decision to block Russian forces from accessing the satellite internet service.
Article Summary: Alex karp backed defense company turning wartime experience into a product for allied countries. Mykhailo fedorov, 35, was removed from his role as defense minister by president volodymyr zelenskyy in july. He has been actively courting u.s. investors and technology executives.

Article Title: Google CEO Sundar Pichai sends a message to his college IIT Kharagpur as it celebrates 75 years; shares happy memories as student: Meals at Harry's, studying in…
Article Text:
Image credit: Instagram

Sundar Pichai's IIT Kharagpur memories: Harry's, Illu and room B-308

Pichai's AI prediction: from labs to farmers, doctors and government offices

IIT Kharagpur at 75: why Pichai is betting on students

Google and Alphabet CEO Sundar Pichai has recorded a video message for IIT Kharagpur as the institute turns 75, and he spends most of it on the small stuff. Meals at Harry's. The Illu festival. Nights spent studying in room B-308. The wingmates, and the professors who stuck with him. Campus, he said, is also where he met his wife Anjali, where he first learned to program, and where he carried floppy disks around to get time on one of the few machines available. "These moments shaped the course of my life," he said, "putting me on a path to Google."That last line is the pivot. The message, posted by IIT Kharagpur on X, works as two things at once—a nostalgia reel and a forecast. Pichai, who graduated in 1993 with a B.Tech in metallurgical engineering, uses the anniversary to set out where he thinks artificial intelligence lands over the next five years, and to make a case that universities, not just tech companies, will decide whether any of it reaches people who aren't already using it.The specificity is what makes it land. B-308 in Nehru Hall is an unremarkable hostel room—bed, study table, chair, almirah—and it has quietly become a campus landmark, currently occupied by a final-year chemical engineering student.Metallurgy, meanwhile, sits nowhere near the top of India's engineering pecking order, which is part of why the room has the pull it does.Pichai called an education from the institute "truly a gift" and said IIT Kharagpur "played a formative role in shaping the lens through which I strive to make an impact on the world." He also noted how far its graduates have travelled, in India and outside it.The forward-looking half is the newsier one. "When I look at the next five years, I see AI moving away from the lab and the early adopters and into the hands of people doing the work," Pichai said—"the healthcare workers, the government officials, the farmers, developers, and entrepreneurs."The framing is deliberate. He is not describing AI as something to experiment with, but as something that sits inside jobs people already do. "We are building AI so that it can help all of us do our work at the next level and do it in a more fulfilling way," he added.It also tracks with where Alphabet has pointed itself. Under Pichai, AI now runs through Search, Cloud and the Gemini family of models a shift the company's own regulatory filings describe as central to its strategy. A prediction about AI spreading into everyday work is, conveniently, also a description of Google's product roadmap.On India, Pichai said the country is increasingly producing innovations that can benefit the whole world, and that an "ambitious, optimistic new generation of Indians" has the chance to reimagine what's possible. AI can amplify that potential, he argued, but universities are what keep it useful to everyone rather than to a narrow few—a point that doubles as the institute's brief for its next 25 years.Much of the current momentum, he said, is coming from students. He recalled meeting Gemini Student Ambassadors from across India at the AI Impact Summit in Delhi this year: "Their enthusiasm for how technology can improve lives was palpable, and it's why I'm so optimistic about the future." The role of IIT Kharagpur, he added, "will only grow in importance as you lead the next wave of technology."The institute responded by calling the message a reflection of "the enduring global impact of the IIT ecosystem," saying it now looks ahead "to nurture ideas, inspire generations and create solutions that make a difference to India and the world."After Kharagpur, Pichai went to Stanford and then Wharton. He joined Google in 2004, worked on Toolbar and Chrome before taking charge of product and engineering across its major platforms, became CEO in 2015, and added Alphabet in December 2019.
Article Summary: Google ceo sundar pichai has recorded a video message for iit kharagpur as the institute turns 75. He uses the anniversary to set out where he thinks artificial intelligence lands over the next five years. He says universities, not just tech companies, will decide whether any of it reaches people who aren't already using it.

Article Title: Apple's new CEO John Ternus may have just told millions of professionals around the world that LinkedIn is 'not important' when you are ...
Article Text:
Limited information on Apple CEO John Ternus’ LinkedIn profile

John Ternus recently joined Twitter

Apple’s new CEO John Ternus may have just told millions of professionals around the world that LinkedIn is 'not important' when you are trying to reach the top of the tech industry. John Ternus became Apple CEO on September 1 after more than 25 years at the company, but his LinkedIn profile still does not list him as CEO. Instead, the profile identifies Ternus as Apple’s vice president of hardware engineering. It also leaves out much of his career at Apple, including his involvement with major products such as the Apple Watch and AirPods.For someone who has risen to lead one of the world’s biggest technology companies, his limited LinkedIn presence is notable.John Ternus’ LinkedIn page contains only a small amount of information about his professional career. It lists his time at Apple and a four-year stint as an engineer at Virtual Research Inc. The profile also mentions his mechanical engineering degree from the University of Pennsylvania. Apart from a profile picture and Apple as a followed interest, there is little else.Most notably, the profile has not yet been updated to show his new position as Apple CEO. Apple’s internal pages were updated immediately after Ternus took over from Tim Cook on September 1.While Ternus has not made much of his LinkedIn profile, he recently joined X (formerly Twitter). His first post was simply “hello.” The post had received over 81 million views and 523,000 likes as of the time of the report.Tesla and X chief Elon Musk replied to Ternu’s Hello post writing, “Congrats!"”before following up with an additional comment noting, “New Apple CEO posting on X”.Notably, Ternus currently follows only three accounts: Apple, Tim Cook and Apple senior vice president of marketing Greg Joswiak.
Article Summary: John ternus became apple ceo on september 1 after more than 25 years at the company. His linkedin profile still does not list him as ceo but as vice president of hardware engineering. The profile also leaves out much of his career at apple, including his involvement with major products such as the apple watch and airpods.

Article Title: Amazon to hire 160,000 temporary workers this festive season
Article Text:
Amazon rejects allegations of consumer harm

Ahead of the upcoming festive season, Amazon India has announced that it has created more than 160,000 seasonal work opportunities across its pan India operations network that supports its ecommerce and quick commerce business. These include direct and indirect work opportunities across 400 cities in India, spanning large metros as well as tier 2 and 3 cities like Varanasi, Kochi, Jalandhar, Ghaziabad, Ranchi, Salem, Gorakhpur, and others. Amazon has created opportunities for thousands of women and associates with disabilities in its network. The new associates will join Amazon’s existing pan-India operations network helping pick, pack, ship, and deliver customer orders safely and reliably while supporting the growing demand during the festive period. Amazon has already onboarded the majority of these associates in preparation for the festive season and has begun providing them with the necessary training.As part of Amazon’s commitment to supporting its associates, even the seasonal associates will have access to the range of safety and welfare programs and benefits that other associates have. This includes benefits like a safe, supportive and inclusive workplace, safety, financial and social security.Through its Samridhi program, Amazon will also support associates joining the company’s operations network ahead of the festive season to enroll on the e-shram portal and access other government welfare and social security programs.“We are committed to providing customers across every pin-code in India with fast and reliable deliveries this festive season. To meet the anticipated increase in customer demand, we have created over 1.6 lakh seasonal work opportunities across our operations network. As we focus on building one of India’s largest, safest, fastest and most reliable operations network, we are also committed to building an inclusive workforce, with opportunities for thousands of women associates and persons with disabilities. This expanded workforce will help us strengthen our fulfillment and logistics capabilities and ensure we can handle the festive season seamlessly. Many of these associates continue their journey with Amazon beyond the festive period, while several others return year after year to work with us,” said Abhinav Singh, VP, Operations, Amazon India, APAC, Middle East, Africa and Turkiye.Amazon India claims to have fulfilment centers spread across 15 states, offering over 43 million cubic feet of storage space for seller inventory; sortation centers in 19 states; along with a network of close to 2,000 Amazon-operated and partner delivery stations. Also, it has 28,000 'Hub delivery' partners and thousands of Amazon Flex partners, who are ready to deliver smiles to customers across the country.
Article Summary: Amazon india has created more than 160,000 seasonal work opportunities across its pan india operations network that supports its ecommerce and quick commerce business. The new associates will join amazon’s existing pan-india operations network helping pick, pack, ship, and deliver customer orders.

Article Title: JioHotstar launches in UK, Canada and Singapore with new shows and live features
Article Text:
JioHotstar launches in UK, Canada and Singapore with new shows and live features

JioHotstar brings 160,000+ hours of Indian entertainment to international audience

JioHotstar subscription plans for UK, Canada and Singapore

JioHotstar has launched in the UK, Canada and Singapore, bringing its Indian entertainment catalogue to audiences outside India. In a press release, the company said that the “launch goes beyond taking JioHotstar’s extensive entertainment catalogue to new markets” and “brings audiences a new way to discover, watch and engage with entertainment combining 160K+ hours of content across 12+ languages and multiple genres with personalized recommendations, interactive features, flexible subscription options and a delightful product experience”.JioHotstar offers content across several categories, including television, films, regional programming, non-fiction, kids' content and anime. The platform's library includes popular shows and originals such as Criminal Justice, Special Ops, Asur, Aarya, Pritam & Pedro, Heartbeat, Kerala Crime Files and Resort.Its film catalogue includes titles such as Dhurandhar, 12th Fail, Chhichhore, Kesari Chapter 2: The Untold Story of Jallianwala Bagh, Kill, Jab We Met and Vaazha. JioHotstar said it plans to add more than 30,000 hours of fresh content every year, giving users access to a continually expanding catalogue. The platform has kicked off its international launch with a diverse line-up of entertainment that includes:New Originals & Blockbuster Premieres: A slate of originals including Ali Baba Aur Chaalis Bhoot, Prince of Mollywood, Part Timers, The Court and more alongside blockbuster movie premieres through the year. Bigg Boss , Now Interactive: The iconic reality franchise Bigg Boss returns across six languages, and for the first time, audiences across Singapore, Canada and the UK will be able to vote LIVE across every edition, giving them the power to actively participate in and influence the game in real time. While audiences in Canada and the UK will have access to the 24x7 LIVE Feed, Canada will also be able to watch Bigg Boss Hindi 7 days ahead of its TV broadcast.A New Game Show Format: Audiences in Canada and Singapore can witness the magic of Anil Kapoor hosting India Ka Top 1 Percent, a new format that tests contestants’ logic and reasoning.Content from JioStar TV Channels with Early Access: Audiences can access content from JioStar television channels, including Star Plus, Colors, Star Vijay, Asianet, Star Jalsha and Star Pravah, with Before-TV access to popular shows in Singapore and Canada, including Anupama, Yeh Rishta Kya Kehlata Hai, Seher Hone Ko Hai, Azhagae Azhagu, while audiences in the UK can watch popular shows simultaneously with their TV broadcast, alongside regional and daily entertainment.JioHotstar is also introducing new quarterly subscription plans across all three markets for the first time. The updated pricing effective 2 nd September across markets is as follows:Commenting on JioHotstar’s international expansion and vision for global streaming, Amit Malhotra, Head – International Business, JioStar, said: “Streaming has spent the last decade competing on the size of its catalogue. We believe the bigger opportunity now is to reimagine how audiences experience entertainment; not just what they watch, but how they discover, engage with and shape the experience in real time. South Asian audiences have a deep connection with Indian entertainment across languages, generations and households. At the same time, audiences globally are increasingly seeking stories and cultures beyond their own. We see an opportunity to build for this broader, underserved global audience - not simply export an Indian streaming service to new markets.”He further added, “As we expand internationally, our ambition is to show what becomes possible when scale, language, cultural diversity, personalisation and deeper audience participation are built into the streaming experience from day one.”

Article Title: Netflix unveils ‘VOID’, an AI model that can change a movie plot
Article Text:
Netflix

How Netflix VOID works







Netflix has unveiled an AI model that can alter the scene. While this is nothing new, Netflix’s model not just remove objects from video, it understands what should happen next, essentially altering the causality. Most object-removal technology leaves a gap where something used to be and/ or fills it with a plausible-looking background. VOID goes a step further: after erasing an object from a scene, it calculates how the surrounding environment should realistically respond to its absence, and in the process it adjusts the behaviour of other elements in the frame accordingly.The model, called VOID, is a vision-language system designed to edit video footage with a level of contextual awareness that sets it apart from several existing tools.For example, imagine this scenario: A movie director has just wrapped up a multi-million dollar action sequence where the star drives straight into a fiery, head-on collision. The cars explode, debris scatters, and the scene is a wrap.But suddenly, there is request to change the scene: The character survives and drive off into the sunset instead. This would mean costly reshoots or millions spent on computer-generated graphics.Netflix’s VOID can alter the scene and digitally erase the collision, the second vehicle, the smoke, and the flying debris. It will then generate new, realistic footage of pristine pavement, making it look as though the main character simply drove down an empty, peaceful road.The AI’s ‘magic’ lies in its grasp of real-world physics. Let us understand this by a different example. If a video shows a person jumping into a pool and splashing water onto the deck, VOID can completely erase the person. It will then intelligently alter the water and the wet concrete, leaving behind a perfectly still, undisturbed pool as if nobody had ever jumped in.“To train the model, we generate a new paired dataset of counterfactual object removals using Kubric and HUMOTO, where removing an object requires altering downstream physical interactions. During inference, a vision-language model identifies regions of the scene affected by the removed object. These regions are then used to guide a video diffusion model that generates physically consistent counterfactual outcomes,” Netflix said.“Experiments on both synthetic and real data show that our approach better preserves consistent scene dynamics after object removal compared to prior video object removal methods,” the company added.Netflix isn’t keeping this powerful tool locked behind studio doors, and made the VOID model available to the public on the AI platform Hugging Face, allowing anyone to download and use it.While there are already several video-altering tools on the market, such as Runway, DiffuEraser, and ProPainter, the Netflix team claims VOID is vastly superior, as per The Register.
Article Summary: Netflix has unveiled an ai model that can alter the scene. While this is nothing new, netflix’s model not just remove objects from video, it understands what should happen next. Most object-removal technology leaves a gap where something used to be and/ or fills it with a plausible-looking background.

Article Title: AI data centers are causing 'stress' not just to tech companies, but also private insurers
Article Text:
Massive investments, growing risks



Unique challenges for data centre insurance companies





AI data centers are reportedly putting new pressure on the insurance industry. According to a CNBC report, experts warn that the rapid growth of these projects is becoming a “stress test” not just for tech companies, but also for private insurers and lenders. Consulting firm McKinsey estimates that global spending on data centers could reach $7 trillion by 2030. As costs rise, tech giants are increasingly relying on private equity, private credit and debt to fund these projects. The scale of investments is creating challenges for insurers.“When you put $10 to $20 billion plus in a single location, it creates capacity issues in the marketplace,” said Tom Harper, data center leader at insurance broker Gallagher as quoted in the CNBC report.He added that the sector has been a “real stress test” over the last few years, as insurers struggle to provide coverage for such large and complex projects. While these facilities are seen as high-quality assets, Harper said insuring them has become difficult due to their size and risk concentration.Private data center deals have crossed $10 billion regularly, with some reaching as high as $40 billion. Companies including Nvidia, Microsoft and BlackRock have already taken part in large investment deals.Rajat Rana, partner at Quinn Emanuel Urquhart & Sullivan, described the scale as unprecedented. “We’re talking about trillions of dollars, and almost going back to the same cycle where there’s almost no transparency about the financing structures — the scale is astronomical,” he said. He added that the boom in AI data centers could be “the largest peacetime investment project in human history.”Experts say the way these projects are financed is adding another layer of risk. Much of the funding is happening through complex and less transparent debt structures. Rana warned that this trend feels like “deja vu,” referring to past financial cycles. He said the lack of transparency could create risks for investors, insurers and pension funds.As stated in the CNBC report, data centers offer unique challenges due to their mix of real estate and advanced technology. Insurers are now designing custom policies to manage these risks. However, challenges remain. Large facilities are often located in areas prone to extreme weather, and they store expensive equipment, sometimes even before installation.Another key concern is the mismatch between the lifespan of data centers and the hardware they use. While data centers can last decades, GPUs — the chips powering AI — typically last around seven years. Rana described this as a “GPU debt treadmill,” saying, “This is almost like a treadmill that these AI data centers are running on.”He explained that companies may need to keep raising debt to upgrade infrastructure as technology evolves.
Article Summary: Private data center deals have crossed $10 billion regularly, with some reaching as high as $40 billion. Mckinsey estimates that global spending on data centers could reach $7 trillion by 2030. Tech giants are increasingly relying on private equity, private credit and debt to fund these projects.

Article Title: Clavicular Viral Controversy: "Trans women are.....": Clavicular’s viral moment with trans women sparks fresh conversation on internet culture
Article Text:
A viral clip featuring Clavicular and trans women is gaining attention for its calm and honest tone. The conversation explores how online language and trends move across communities. Instead of conflict, the exchange highlights shared influence and mutual awareness. Viewers are engaging with its thoughtful nature, as it reflects how internet culture evolves through collaboration rather than ownership.

Clavicular and trans women share a surprising realization about online trends







The video of Clavicular, a short-video producer, is going around the Internet, yet not the reason why. There is no yelling or over-the-top drama. It is a mere, everyday talk that seems almost novel nowadays, in the age of internet, which is overflowing with content. The scene is easy-going, the tone of the narrative is straightforward, and the characters appear more concerned with conversation than combat.The message that is being addressed is the flow of the conversation. It discusses internet culture, the way people communicate with one another and the place of trends. Rather than bringing out a debate, the encounter towards curiosity. It quietly brings attention to something that a lot of people who use the internet notice but don't often say out loud. People in different communities often have a bigger impact on each other than they think.The conversation begins with a confident and lighthearted comment from one of the trans women present. She says, "You know that trans women are like the OG lip masters, right? We are very talented in the program. Like, I do the peptides, I'm on Zeta." Her tone carries a mix of pride and humor, setting a relaxed vibe at the table.Clavicular responds in a way that keeps the mood steady but adds a different angle.He says, "That is funny because you guys were using a lot of the words in like the South Korean subreddits in like 2014." It’s not confrontational. If anything, it feels like an observation. He points to how certain words and ideas may have traveled across different online spaces over time.Another voice joins in and brings the moment full circle. "Guys, we're like the OGs. I saw a couple of posts about that. We're like copying each other." That line hits in a simple but honest way. It reflects something familiar. Online culture is rarely created in isolation. It grows through sharing, borrowing, and sometimes even unknowingly repeating.That's what makes the clip so powerful. It doesn't want to make a point or win an argument. It only shows a group of people talking, listening, and figuring something out together.This moment feels different in a space where viral content often leads to fights. It reminds people that conversations can be calm, thoughtful, and still important. And sometimes, that honest silence is what makes it work.
Article Summary: A viral clip featuring clavicular and trans women is gaining attention for its calm and honest tone. The conversation explores how online language and trends move across communities. Viewers are engaging with its thoughtful nature, as it reflects how internet culture evolves through collaboration rather than ownership.

Article Title: Watch: 'Driverless' car crashes into police van after internet outage in Islamabad
Article Text:
In a social media post on Monday, Aalijah sought to clarify that his video was not intended to ridicule Zafar or undermine his work and warned that the technology was not yet ready to be considered completely reliable.

A remotely operated driverless car crashed into a police van in Islamabad after losing its internet connection during a demonstration, with footage of the incident going viral and sparking a wave of memes online.According to local media, the incident took place at D-Chowk, a high-security area in the Pakistani capital, where journalist Muhammad Aalijah was recording a video of a technology-based automated-driving system developed by Abbottabad-based technology enthusiast Ehsan Zafar. The car was being controlled remotely over the internet when a sudden connectivity failure caused its steering to malfunction.Footage shared by Aalijah shows him sitting in the front passenger seat as he explains the vehicle's features while it moves along the road. The remotely controlled steering wheel then appears to lose control, sending the car towards a police van parked nearby.Aalijah can be seen attempting to stop the vehicle by pulling the handbrake, but the car continues moving and bumps into the police vehicle.Aalijah later told Dawn that he had been asked by Zafar to report on his technology-based automated-driving innovation. He attributed the crash to a "technical fault" triggered by an internet disruption.“Everything was fine until a technical fault occurred due to an internet disruption, causing the car to go out of control and crash into a police vehicle,” he said.According to Aalijah, the vehicle was operated remotely through internet and satellite connections. The loss of the internet connection during the demonstration caused the car to become uncontrollable.In a social media post on Monday, Aalijah sought to clarify that his video was not intended to ridicule Zafar or undermine his work.“The sole purpose was to raise awareness and urge people to remain cautious until any new experiment or technology has been thoroughly tested, proven safe and established as a complete success,” he said.“This was a message of caution, not an attempt to discredit anyone.”Aalijah also warned that the technology was not yet ready to be considered completely reliable.“The vehicle was being operated through satellite and internet connections, but during external control, it went out of control as soon as the internet connection was disconnected and collided with a police vehicle,” he wrote.He said the relatively low traffic at D-Chowk limited the potential consequences of the malfunction, but warned that a similar failure on a busy road could have been far more serious.“If the same situation had occurred on a busy road, the consequences could have been extremely dangerous, even fatal,” he said.“This video is not criticism; it is a responsible effort to raise awareness and issue a warning by all means, experiment, but ensure safety first,” he added.
Article Summary: A remotely operated driverless car crashed into a police van in islamabad after losing its internet connection during a demonstration. Footage of the incident went viral and sparked a wave of memes online. Journalist muhammad aalijah was recording a video of a technology-based automated-driving system developed by abbottabad-based technology enthusiast ehsan zafar.

Article Title: UK NHS boss: Britain should learn from India’s healthcare system
Article Text:
Britain should learn from India’s healthcare system, the chair of NHS England Dr Penny Dash has said

LONDON: Britain should learn from India’s healthcare system, the chair of NHS England, Dr Penny Dash, has said, pointing out India may soon set the global standard that others want to emulate.“India, oh my goodness... India is just off,” Dash, who has one of the top jobs in global healthcare, told the HealthTech Hour podcast.“I think India is probably going to become the global exemplar in healthcare provision,” she said.“As in many other things, they love their tech and so technology in healthcare in India…yes, there is some cool stuff happening in the US… But India is just off and they are using technology in ways that the US could only dream of, and we can only dream of and, more which is of interest to us, they are doing it in a way which democratises access to healthcare and they feel very strongly about that.”She said founders of tech firms in India and managers and doctors working in healthcare delivery also feel this way.Dash’s praise for India’s ability to deliver high-quality care to vast numbers of patients at scale through technology comes as the NHS attempts to improve productivity and digitise to manage a growing and aging population.Through the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission, India has built one of the largest public digital health frameworks in the world, and its eSanjeevani platform has facilitated hundreds of millions of teleconsultations.Meanwhile, AI is being used in India to detect diseases and predict localised malaria and dengue outbreaks.“By using technology you can reduce the unit cost of care,” Dash said. “Technology now was standardised operating processes 20 years ago. In India they were very early in standardised operating processes and now tech has enabled those standardised operating processes and so they are delivering outstandingly good healthcare for dramatically lower unit costs than almost anyone else currently. So, wow is the main thing. That’s going to be very interesting. Watch that space,” Dash said.
Article Summary: Nhs england chair dr penny dash says britain should learn from india’s healthcare system. Dash: “i think india is probably going to become the global exemplar in healthcare provision.” india has built one of the largest public digital health frameworks in the world.

Article Title: ChatGPT is first AI chatbot to face tougher EU rules
Article Text:
ChatGPT is first AI chatbot to face tougher EU rules﻿

ChatGPT will have to comply with tougher safety rules after the EU added it Monday to a list of digital services subject to greater legal scrutiny, a first for an AI chatbot.Brussels also designated Reddit and Roblox as “very large” online platforms, a label that comes with additional obligations and oversight. “ChatGPT, Reddit and Roblox will now be held to a higher standard of scrutiny and accountability in the EU, in line with their large impact on our citizens and society,” EU technology chief Henna Virkkunen said.The designation applies to platforms and search engines with over 45 million monthly active users in the 27-nation bloc, a threshold the three platforms reported meeting, the commission said. The three now have four months to comply with additional obligations under the Digital Services Act, a content law the EU has deployed to rein in Big Tech.
Article Summary: Chatgpt is first ai chatbot to face tougher eu rules. Reddit and roblox also designated as ‘very large’ online platforms. The three now have four months to comply with additional obligations under the digital services act.
